# Qora v0.34 — complete language reference for AI assistants

Qora is a quantum programming language (Q#/C#-flavored syntax) that compiles to OpenQASM 3.
File extension: `.qor`. This file is the full, authoritative surface spec: everything below is
implemented and everything not mentioned does not exist. When generating Qora code, use ONLY the
constructs listed here.

Docs: https://aj-comp.github.io/Qora/  ·  Repo: https://github.com/AJ-comp/Qora
VS Code extension: `qora-lang.qora-language` (bundles the compiler; errors as you type).

## Compilation model

- One entry file compiles to one OpenQASM 3 program: `qora --json main.qor`.
  No project files. `import` statements load other files (transitively, relative to the importing
  file). Everything merges into one program before name resolution.
- The operation named `Main` (in the global namespace) is the entry point: its body becomes the
  QASM top level. Every other operation becomes a `def`. If no `Main` exists, the first operation
  is the entry.
- Compilation is all-or-nothing: any diagnostic blocks emission. Each reached stage reports all
  violations it collects, but a failing stage prevents later stages from running. Located diagnostics
  use a half-open, document-qualified `SourceSpan`, so an imported document's offsets are never
  interpreted as entry-file offsets.
- Library API boundary: `QoraParser.Parse` returns a syntax-only `SyntaxSnapshot`; use
  `QoraCompiler.Compile` for semantic analysis, MIR, diagnostics, and target output. The latter returns
  one immutable `Compilation`, whose authoritative owners are `Sources`, `Hir`, optional `Mir`,
  `Links`, `Targets`, and `Diagnostics`. `Sources` preserves every root/import
  `SourceDocumentSnapshot`, its exact `SyntaxSnapshot`, and revision-qualified `ImportGraph` edges.
  A public syntax snapshot contains only Qora-owned immutable token/tree projections, captured tree
  text, and diagnostics. The mutable Janglim AST lives only in an internal transient
  `SyntaxParseProduct` and is discarded immediately after per-document HIR lowering.
  The internal `SourceGraphLoader` owns import I/O and per-document parsing/lowering;
  `ModuleLoader` only merges that prepared graph and never reads or reparses files. Its result also
  classifies every imported HIR node with a document-qualified `HirNodeIntroduction`.
- `CompilationSession` owns one logical compilation identity and allocates monotonically unique
  revisions. `Compilation.ParentRevision` records the actual recompile parent, so two children of the
  same snapshot receive different revisions without losing their shared ancestry. `QoraCompiler.Compile`
  starts a new session; `QoraCompiler.Recompile` asks the previous snapshot's session for a child.
- `CompilationOptions.OutputPlan` is the immutable requested-output contract. It records the exact
  `HirCompilationGoal`, whether MIR is required, and the backend set. A successful compilation must
  contain exactly those requested MIR/target artifacts and no unsolicited ones. The current canonical
  HIR goal is `EffectAnalyzedCanonical`; `CompilationOutputPlan.HirOnly` requests no MIR or target,
  while `Default` requests MIR plus OpenQASM.
- A `HirSnapshot` contains one immutable structural `HirProgram` declaration/expression tree and its
  source map. Validation and effect facts
  are separate, exact-snapshot `HirSemanticArtifact` values. A validation artifact always owns one
  immutable `HirValidationOutcome`: `Accepted` has no diagnostics, while `Rejected` owns the exact
  diagnostics that caused rejection. Compilation diagnostics only add stage/origin metadata to that
  outcome; they are not a second validation truth. Effect analysis accepts only the exact accepted
  validation artifact for the same snapshot and records it as `ValidationBasis`. Analysis does not create another
  structural HIR stage. Query the effect artifact as `Compilation.Hir.EffectAnalysis`. The canonical
  milestone order is `Lowered -> ImportsExpanded -> Resolved -> Specialized`;
  a no-op pass may alias its predecessor but may not move a later milestone backwards. HIR has no
  conjugation or adjoint stage.
  `HirCompilation` also owns the exact `HirLineage` over those same snapshot objects. Identity-preserving
  `NodeDerivation`, provenance-only `NodeSynthesis`, and source `HirNodeIntroduction` are distinct typed
  classifications. Every node newly appearing after the first snapshot must have exactly one of them.
  Semantic lookup follows only identity-preserving edges; provenance queries may follow synthesis.
  `Compilation.Mir` is a separate typed SSA/CFG snapshot with revision-bound analyses. Core retains
  only the exact final HIR `LoweringSource` and the program-owned `Origins` required by compilation,
  diagnostics, transformations, and target lowering; it does not own an IDE-oriented symbol-to-MIR
  index. `Qora.LanguageServices` may opt into a compile-call-scoped lowering trace and publish an
  immutable, exact-revision `MirSemanticIndex`, while ordinary compilation allocates no such index.
  MIR stages are `Lowered -> InverseRequestsInjected -> AdjointsMaterialized`; each transformed
  snapshot records its exact parent and rebases its origin table.
- `Compilation.Targets.Artifacts` is the authoritative backend-keyed target map;
  `Compilation.Targets.OpenQasm` is the current typed convenience view. The OpenQASM artifact records
  the exact materialized `MirSnapshot` it consumed. The backend never reaches back into HIR or its
  semantic model, and target diagnostics carry the backend plus an exact MIR input identity. A failed compilation
  retains every artifact already published before the failure, while later artifacts and successful
  target output are absent. `QasmBackend` accepts only an exact `MirSnapshot`, produces a
  `MirOpenQasmTargetProgram`, and `OpenQasmArtifact.Text` is then derived from that target model by the
  pure emitter; emitted text is not an independent authoritative input.
- In the emitted QASM, user-defined names pass through unchanged when they are already safe.
  Namespaces flatten dots with `_` (`MyLib.Bell` -> `MyLib_Bell`), and `_` is appended only when
  an emitted identifier would collide with a keyword, stdgates gate, or another emitted name.
  Rename notes appear as `// Qora:` comments in the QASM header.

## Program structure

```qora
import "gates_lib.qor";         // quoted relative path, resolved from this file's directory
import "lib/gates.qor";         // subdirectory path; extension included
import "a b.qor";               // spaces are fine inside the quoted path

namespace MyLib                 // optional; may be dotted: namespace A.B
{
    open OtherLib;              // unqualified access to OtherLib's callables (namespace-scope only)
    function two(): int { return 2; }
    operation Bell(q: Qubit[])
    {
        H(q[0]);
        CNOT(q[0], q[1]);
    }
}

operation Main()                // global namespace; the entry point; takes NO parameters
{
    use q = Qubit[2];           // qubit allocation: ONLY in the entry op, top level only
    MyLib.Bell(q);              // qualified call
    var n: int = MyLib.two();   // qualified function call is also valid in an expression
    var r: bit = M(q[0]);       // measurement (the only way to get a bit)
    if (r == 1) { X(q[1]); }
}
```

## Types and declarations

- Type annotations are TRAILING: `name: Type` (a parameter `q: Qubit[]`, a variable `var x: int = 5`).
  The type comes AFTER the name, introduced by `:`.
- `q: Qubit` is a single-qubit parameter. `q: Qubit[]` is a register parameter whose length is supplied
  by the caller; use `q.Count` inside the operation. The compiler specializes the operation for each
  concrete register size before emitting OpenQASM.
- `int`, `float`, `bit`, `angle` are classical scalar types. Measurement produces a `bit`, which holds
  a 0/1 result.
- `use name = Qubit[N];` — allocate a register. Entry operation only, not inside loops/branches.
- Classical arrays use `int[]`, `float[]`, `bit[]`, or `angle[]`. Declare them anywhere a scalar
  declaration goes — `Main`, helper operations, loops, branches — either with a non-empty literal
  (`var xs: int[] = [1, 2, 3];`) or a positive literal-sized, zero-initialized allocation
  (`var xs: int[] = new int[3];`); the compiler handles OpenQASM's global-scope rule automatically. Helper
  operations may also receive matching `T[]` parameters. Read/write elements with `xs[i]`, and read
  the length with `xs.Count`.
- An index is a full expression whose result must be one scalar `int`: `xs[i + 1]`, `xs[idx()]`, and
  `q[choose(k)]` all parse and use ordinary function name/signature/type resolution. OpenQASM emission
  still requires an in-bounds proof. A function result is not currently evaluated at compile time, so
  `xs[idx()]` is QSEM030 unless it is evaluated once into an `int` variable and that variable is guarded,
  for example `var i: int = idx(); if (0 <= i && i < xs.Count) { var x: int = xs[i]; }`.
- A WHOLE `bit[]` register is a CONTAINER OF BITS, not a number. A bit pattern carries no sign, so
  the same bits read 2 unsigned and -2 in two's complement; the language will not pick one silently.
  Using a whole register as a number is QSEM036: `var n: int = f;`, `f + 1`, `if (f)`, `f == 1`, and
  ordering (`f < g`). Legal without any numeric reading: `f[i]`, `f.Count`, passing `f` as an argument,
  and `f == g` / `f != g` between registers OF THE SAME WIDTH (compared as bit patterns, emitted bare).
  To read a register as a number, write `AsInt(f)` — the one explicit unsigned reading, emitted as the
  width-qualified `uint[N](f)`. A SCALAR `bit` (one measurement result) is unaffected: it is a value, and
  `r == 1` emits as `r == true`.
- Operation resource parameters have two independent call-boundary axes: OWNERSHIP is borrowed by default
  or transferred with `move`, while ACCESS is read-only by default or mutable with `var`. The declaration
  and call site must state the same contract:

  | Syntax | Ownership | Access |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `values` | borrowed | read-only |
  | `var values` | borrowed | mutable |
  | `move values` | transferred | read-only |
  | `move var values` | transferred | mutable |

  For example, declare `operation Increment(var values: int[])` and call `Increment(var values)`.
- The supported combinations depend on storage shape. `var` and `move var` require a whole
  `int[]`/`float[]`/`angle[]`, because those are the caller-visible mutable reference types in the current
  backend. Read-only `move` accepts any whole array (including `bit[]` and `Qubit[]`) and a whole single
  `Qubit` binding. Classical scalars are Copy values and reject `move`; mutable bit/qubit parameters reject
  `var`. Every `function` parameter uses only the default borrowed/read-only contract. Qubit state changes
  through gates continue to follow Qora's quantum-state rules, while `move` controls whether the caller may
  use that qubit binding again.
- A mutable borrow (`var`) requires mutable caller storage, so a `const` array cannot be passed with
  `var` (QSEM024). `move var` is different: it transfers the binding instead of borrowing it, so a
  `const` binding MAY be passed with `move var` and becomes mutable under its new owner. After either
  `move` form, the caller must not read, write, borrow, or move that binding again; any such use is
  QSEM039.
- Read-only borrowed array arguments may alias each other. A mutable borrow or ownership transfer is
  exclusive, so the same storage cannot also occupy another argument position in that call (QSEM014).
  A borrowed parameter cannot be forwarded with `move`, because it does not own the storage. Whole-array
  reassignment is not supported; a mutable operation updates individual elements instead.
- Every declaration begins with `var` (mutable) or `const` (immutable); the type is optional and trailing.
  `var x = expr;` / `var x: int = expr;` — mutable variable. `const x = expr;` / `const x: int = expr;` —
  IMMUTABLE binding (JS-const/Q#-let style): may hold any value including a measurement result
  (`const r = M(q[0]);`), but can never be assigned again (QSEM024).
- When the type is omitted, the declaration keeps the initializer's semantic type through emission.
  Literals, referenced variables, operators, array elements, and function calls use the same rule:
  `var truth = true` is `bit`, `var copy = anAngle` is `angle`, and `var x = f()` uses `f`'s return type.
- `var r: bit = M(q[i]);` — measure qubit i into a fresh bit. `r = M(q[i]);` re-measures.
  A whole declaration/assignment RHS may instead use `M(a)` when `a` is one `Qubit`. An indexed
  measurement is also legal inside an `if`/`while`/`repeat` condition as `M(q[i])`; the common lowering
  pass hoists it to a fresh bit at the condition's evaluation point. Measurement is not a value for
  ordinary arithmetic or call arguments (measure into a bit first).
- An `operation` is void (no return value); its call is a STATEMENT only. To return a value, use a
  `function` (see below). Qubit allocation sizes and `new T[N]` array lengths must be positive literal integers.

## Functions (classical, value-returning)

- `function Name(params): T { … return e; }` — a classical, pure subroutine (Q#'s `function`). Parameters
  are read-only classical scalars or arrays and accept only the default borrowed/read-only spelling;
  `var`, `move`, and `move var` are not allowed. The return type `T` is a classical scalar
  (`int`/`bit`/`float`/`angle`); neither may be a qubit. A `bit[]` parameter is specialized to the concrete
  argument width at every expression call site, so width-2 and width-3 calls receive separate generated
  definitions while repeated calls of the same width reuse one. The body is
  PURE: only classical statements (`var`/`const`/`if`/`for`/`while`), calls to OTHER functions, and `return`.
  A function may NOT apply a gate, `use` qubits, measure, or call an operation (QSEM033).
- Because a function is pure, its CALL is a value — usable anywhere in an expression: an initializer
  (`var k: int = two();`), an assignment RHS, a gate argument (`Rx(angleOf(k), q[0])`), a condition
  (`if (c == g()) { … }`), or another function's body (`return inner(y) + 1;`). An `operation` call has no
  value (QSEM005); only a function's does.
- Function calls follow the same namespace rules as operation calls. Inside `namespace L`, `two()` first
  searches `L`; `open Other;` makes `Other.two()` available as `two()` when it is the only match; and
  `L.two()` may be written explicitly in any expression position.
- A `return` may stand ANYWHERE a statement may — an early return, a return inside `if`/`else`, a return
  inside a `for`/`while`. The compiler rewrites the function into the single-bottom-return form the execution
  target needs; you never write around that. A function must still `return` on every path (a lone `if` with no
  `else` and nothing after it does not) — QSEM035 otherwise. Recursion is not allowed
  (QSEM011), same as operations.
- Every returned value must be compatible with the function's declared return type (QSEM037). The same
  signature supplies the type of an untyped result: `var x = f();` gives `x` the declared return type of `f`.
  A whole array is never one scalar value, and an incompatible function result cannot be stored in an
  explicitly typed scalar.
- Example:
  ```qora
  function angleOf(k: int): angle { return pi / k; }
  operation Main() {
      use q = Qubit[1];
      Rx(angleOf(4), q[0]);
      var r: bit = M(q[0]);
  }
  ```

## Statements

- Gate/operation call: `Name(args);` — qubits as `q` (whole register) or `q[i]`.
- `if (cond) { } else { }` (else-if allowed). Conditions: == != < <= > >= && || ! over bits/ints.
- `for i in start..stop { }` — inclusive range; bounds are expressions, so
  `for i in 0..values.Count-1 { }` is valid.
- `while (cond) { }` · `repeat { } until (cond);`
- Comments: `//` to end of line. (No block comments.)

## Built-in gates (complete list; case-sensitive)

- 1-qubit: `H X Y Z S T` — e.g. `H(q[0]);`
- 2-qubit: `CNOT CX CY CZ SWAP` — e.g. `CNOT(q[0], q[1]);` (CNOT and CX are the same gate)
- 3-qubit: `CCX`
- Rotations (ANGLE FIRST): `Rx Ry Rz` — e.g. `Rx(pi/2, q[0]);` Constants: `pi`, `tau`, `euler`.
- Reset: `Reset(q[0]);` `ResetAll(q);` — statements, not gates: no functors on them.
- Measurement: `M(q[i])` in the assignment forms above. `Measure`/`measure` are NOT valid.

## Functors

- `Controlled G(ctrl, ...args);` — adds a control qubit (FIRST argument). Built-in gates only,
  never on user operations (QSEM002).
- There is no source-level inverse/Adjoint functor, and HIR has no inverse marker or conjugation node.
  An internal MIR scheduler may attach `MirFunctor.Adjoint` only to an exact `MirQuantumApply`;
  `MirAdjointMaterializer` consumes that MIR-only request.

## Name resolution (C#/Q# rules)

For an unqualified call inside namespace `A.B`, in order:
1. `A.B`'s own operations/functions; 2. containing namespace `A`; 3. the global namespace;
4. namespaces opened by exact namespace `A.B` — exactly one open candidate wins, two+ is QSEM018
(qualify to fix), and zero falls through to QSEM007.
- Qualified names (`MyLib.Bell`, `MyLib.two()`, `A.B.f()`) are absolute and walk every namespace
  segment from the program root in statement and expression calls. `open A` exposes only A's direct
  callables: it does not expose `A.B`, inherit a containing namespace's opens, or re-export what A opened.
  `open` does NOT load files (import does). Namespaces merge across files; the same operation name twice
  in one namespace is QSEM022 (in the global namespace, QSEM008).
- A dotted namespace creates one symbol per segment, so declaring `namespace A.B` makes `A` a valid
  namespace too; opening A still does not expose B's members. Namespace and callable members with the
  same spelling can coexist because intermediate path segments select namespaces and call endpoints
  select callables.
- Built-in gates live in the implicit namespace `Qora.Intrinsic` (always open). A NAMESPACED
  operation may reuse a gate name (`namespace L { operation Rx ... }`); an unqualified use that
  could mean both is QSEM018 — write `L.Rx(...)` or `Qora.Intrinsic.Rx(...)`. Global operations
  may NOT take gate names (QSEM013). Reserved everywhere: `M`, `Measure`, `measure`, `pi`, `tau`,
  `euler`, `AsInt`, and declaring namespace `Qora.Intrinsic`.

## Error codes (collect-all within each reached stage; located errors carry a source span)

QSEM001 compiler-generated inverse target not invertible (internal defensive diagnostic)
QSEM002 Controlled on a user operation        QSEM003 functor on Reset/ResetAll
QSEM004 bare measurement statement            QSEM005 void/measurement call used in an unsupported value position
QSEM006 wrong argument count/kind/type for a call
QSEM007 unknown gate/operation name           QSEM008 duplicate global callable name
QSEM009 calling the entry operation           QSEM010 entry operation has parameters
QSEM011 recursive callable calls              QSEM012 `use` outside the entry operation's top level
QSEM013 name shadows a built-in where qualification cannot disambiguate
QSEM014 same qubit (or overlapping register/element) twice in one gate; overlapping exclusive storage access
QSEM015 duplicate declared names in one operation
QSEM016 non-integer or proven-out-of-range array/qubit index / indexing a scalar or single qubit
QSEM017 measurement assigned to a non-bit     QSEM018 ambiguous unqualified name (candidates listed)
QSEM019 unknown namespace/member in qualified name or `open`
QSEM020 import file not found/unreadable/no file context
QSEM021 retired/reserved; cyclic back-edges reuse the canonical `SourceDocumentRef` and are visited once
QSEM022 duplicate callable name within one namespace
QSEM023 reserved; emitted-name collisions are auto-renamed by `MirOpenQasmLowering`
QSEM024 mutation of a `const` value/array, including a `var` mutable borrow (not `move var`)
QSEM025 identifier not declared in scope here (unknown name, or classical used before declaration)
QSEM026 qubit used as a classical value       QSEM027 retired (source/HIR conjugation was removed)
QSEM028 operation name used as a value
QSEM029 invalid array shape, initializer, member, or whole-array assignment
QSEM030 OpenQASM target cannot emit an index whose in-bounds proof remains unresolved
QSEM031 expression or nested-block structure exceeds the compiler depth limit
QSEM032 write to a `bit[]` parameter (OpenQASM passes bit registers by value)
QSEM033 impure function body (a gate, `use`, measurement, or operation call inside a function)
QSEM034 a qubit in a function signature (function parameters/return are classical)
QSEM035 `return` outside a function (an operation is void), or a function has a path that returns nothing
QSEM036 a whole `bit[]` register used as a number, compared across widths, or ordered (use `AsInt(f)`)
QSEM037 incompatible function return/result type, or a whole classical array used as one scalar
QSEM038 invalid ownership/access contract (unsupported shape, marker mismatch, or read-only mutation)
QSEM039 use of a caller binding after its ownership was transferred with `move`
QSEM040 the program contains no callable at all, or contains functions but no runnable operation

## CLI contract (for tooling/agents)

```
qora --json [file] [--stages] [--base-dir <dir>] [--source-path <path>]
```
- Source from `file` or stdin (UTF-8). Imports resolve next to `file`, or against `--base-dir`
  for stdin. Reply: ONE line of JSON:
  `{"success":bool,"qasm":"...","errors":[{"message","code","start","end","path","document"}]}`
  `start`/`end` are half-open character offsets in the exact source `path`; `document` is the
  compilation-revision-qualified document identity. `--source-path` supplies that identity's path when
  live source text is sent on stdin.
- `--stages` adds `"ast"`, `"ir"`, `"symbols"`, `"uncompute"`, `"mir"`, and `"mirEffects"`.
  `ir` is the resolved source-shaped HIR; `mir` is the typed SSA/CFG analysis form; both keep
  original/FQN source names unmangled. These views are read from the same completed immutable
  `Compilation`; the CLI does not rerun compiler passes to reconstruct them. A stage not reached
  because of an earlier error is returned as an empty string.
- Emitted QASM starts with `// generated by Qora v0.34`.

## Executing programs

- Full language (def/int/for/while): `python tools/run_braket.py file.qor --shots 1000` — runs on
  Amazon Braket's LOCAL simulator (pip install amazon-braket-sdk, Python 3.10-3.13). Keep
  tools/stdgates.inc next to the working directory (the script handles this).
- Qiskit (`qiskit.qasm3.loads`): accepts only the FLAT subset — no `def`, no `int` declarations,
  no variable qubit indices. Programs with operations/loops/variables will not load there today.

## Complete examples

Bell + measurement (minimal program):
```qora
operation Main() {
    use q = Qubit[2];
    H(q[0]);
    CNOT(q[0], q[1]);
    var r0: bit = M(q[0]);
    var r1: bit = M(q[1]);
}
```

Caller-owned classical array updated by a helper:
```qora
operation Increment(var values: int[]) {
    for i in 0..values.Count-1 { values[i] = values[i] + 1; }
}
operation Main() {
    var values: int[] = [1, 2, 3];
    Increment(var values);
}
```

Multi-file (lib.qor + main.qor):
```qora
// lib.qor
namespace Lib {
    operation Flip(q: Qubit) { X(q); }
}
// main.qor
import "lib.qor";
operation Main() {
    use q = Qubit[1];
    Lib.Flip(q[0]);
}
```

## Common mistakes to avoid

- `use` inside a non-entry operation or inside a loop/branch (QSEM012) — allocate in Main, pass
  qubits as parameters.
- A measurement inside arithmetic or a call argument, such as `Rx(M(q[0]), q[1])` (QSEM005) —
  measure into a bit first. An indexed measurement directly inside a condition is supported.
- `var n: int = f;` / `f + 1` / `if (f)` / `f == 1` on a `bit[]` (QSEM036) — a whole register is not a
  number; write `AsInt(f)`. (A single bit `f[i]` is already a value and needs no conversion.)
- `Rx(q[0], pi/2)` (QSEM006) — rotations take the ANGLE first.
- `qubit` lowercase as a type — the keyword is `Qubit` (capital Q).
- Type BEFORE the name (`int n`, `Qubit[] q`) — annotations are trailing: `n: int`, `q: Qubit[]`.
- Writing an ordinary array parameter, omitting `var` at either the declaration or call site, or adding an
  unsupported mode to a function/scalar slot (QSEM038) — the operation declaration and call must use the same
  `x` / `var x` / `move x` / `move var x` contract.
- Using an array or qubit binding after passing it with `move` or `move var` (QSEM039) — ownership has left the caller.
  A `const` array cannot be borrowed with `var`, but it may be transferred with `move var`.
- `q: Qubit[2]` as a parameter — register parameters omit the length: `q: Qubit[]`; allocate the
  concrete size in `Main` with `use q = Qubit[2];`.
- Calling `Main` (QSEM009), giving `Main` parameters (QSEM010), recursion (QSEM011).
- Expecting `open` to load a file — only `import` loads; `open` shortens names.
